clue.text: With less hair, daughter has changed? Poppycock

indicators.note: something changed has been altered, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

parts.note: having less hair means being more bald
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
the three letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that a daughter's thinning hair means she has changed.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark ends the wordplay; the single last word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal synonyms for nonsense or foolish talk.

clue.text: Attempt made by Ballesteros, initially with wood

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the golfer's name just before it

parts.note: the first letter of the golfer's surname
ash is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: Golfer Seve Ballesteros tries a shot with a wooden club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood' looks like a golf club in the surface, but it is a tree's timber here.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a bash at something is an informal British idiom for making a try.

clue.text: Rings about predicament caused by gaps in the law

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rings go around the predicament

parts.note: loops are rings or circles
to be in a hole is to be in a predicament

explanation.surface: Bell-ringing about some legal trouble arising from flaws in legislation.
explanation.definitionFit: A loophole is an ambiguity or omission in a statute that lets someone evade its intent.

clue.text: Complete set of religious books found in Ireland

indicators.note: found in places one piece inside the other, the country wrapping the books

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A full collection of scripture discovered somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire and complete are adjective synonyms meaning whole, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Play in unsafe spot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a 1932 drama by J. B. Priestley
second meaning: a risky bend or place, taken literally

explanation.walkthrough: The play title is J. B. Priestley's well-known 1932 drama; read literally the same phrase is a hazardous place.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a stage work, and the literal phrase describes a perilous turn in a road.

clue.text: So, in Sweden, grasp changes and make full use of one's talents

definitions.text: make full use of one's talents

indicators.note: changes tells us the preceding words are altered into a new order

parts.note: all fifteen letters of these words, used as fodder

explanation.surface: A Swedish grip alters, letting someone reach their full potential.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, drawn from a young bird first flying, means to venture out and exploit one's abilities.

clue.text: Endless industrial action in a Scandinavian capital

indicators.note: endless means both ends are cut off, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a go-slow is a form of industrial action where workers deliberately slow down

explanation.surface: Workers in a Nordic capital stage a never-ending strike.
explanation.walkthrough: A go-slow is a British protest where staff work slowly on purpose; strip its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the seat of government of Norway, one of the Scandinavian countries.

clue.text: Commotion about a single step

indicators.note: about means around, so the commotion surrounds the single item

parts.note: a stir is a fuss or commotion
a, meaning one, taken as written

explanation.surface: A great fuss is made over one small move.
explanation.definitionFit: A single tread in a flight of steps is a stair, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Easily defeated (KO'd) — Edward after lesson

indicators.note: after sets the name behind the schoolroom word, so the lesson comes first and Edward second

parts.note: a boxer who is KO'd (knocked out) is out
a class is a lesson at school
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A boxer called Edward was flattened after training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the name behind the lesson; the bracketed KO'd is wordplay, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outclassed is to be beaten by a far superior opponent, hence defeated with ease.

clue.text: Cut down others growing wild at end of garden

indicators.note: plants growing wild spread in no order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder

indicators.note: end of picks out only the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter of garden

explanation.surface: Pruning back the other plants rampaging at the bottom of the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten something is to reduce its length, which is what cutting down does.

clue.text: Batter and split bulwark

parts.note: to ram is to batter or strike hard
to part is to split or separate

explanation.surface: Attackers pound and breach a defensive wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampart is a defensive earthen wall around a fort, which is exactly a bulwark.

clue.text: To get on in fashion I start to travel

parts.note: fashion used as a verb, meaning to create or build
taken as written

indicators.note: start to points to the opening letter of the word after it

parts.note: the first letter of travel

explanation.surface: Someone hoping to succeed in the fashion world sets off on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fashion' reads as one phrase about style, but 'in' is only the link and 'fashion' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To make it is an idiom for succeeding in life, the same as getting on.

clue.text: Fish in lock, here? Reams, improbably

indicators.note: improbably suggests an unlikely arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: all thirteen letters of these words, used as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that reams of fish could be found in this canal lock.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse mackerel, or scad, is a species of sea fish found in European waters.

clue.text: Vile place? Bed is, if poorly

indicators.note: poorly means badly or ill, so the letters are put in a bad order

parts.note: all ten letters of these words, used as fodder

explanation.surface: A grim lodging, if the bed in it is shoddily made.
explanation.definitionFit: Despicable means deserving contempt, so it is an adjective synonym for vile.

clue.text: They may be inside creel, slithering

definitions.text: They may be inside creel, slithering

indicators.note: inside tells us to look within the run of letters that follows

parts.note: letters running across the two words, crEEL Slithering

explanation.surface: Wriggling creatures caught in a fisherman's basket.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the description: a creel is a wicker fishing basket.
explanation.definitionFit: These snakelike fish slither and are traditionally caught in wicker traps or baskets.

clue.text: Attend works and have a breakdown

parts.note: to go to an event is to attend it
pieces are works of art or music

explanation.surface: Someone visits a factory and suffers a collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' looks like a factory, but it means artistic compositions.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to pieces is an idiom for losing emotional control and falling apart.

clue.text: Poet led corgi out over top of Exmoor

indicators.note: out suggests being disordered, so those words are scrambled

parts.note: the eight letters used as fodder

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of the moorland name

parts.note: the first letter of Exmoor

explanation.surface: A poet walked his corgi across Exmoor.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'over' puts the scrambled letters above the single letter. Coleridge lived near Exmoor, a moorland in south-west England, when he wrote Kubla Khan.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Taylor Coleridge was the English Romantic writer of The Rime of the Ancient Mariner.

clue.text: Entertains in the morning on manoeuvres

parts.note: a.m. denotes the morning hours
to manoeuvre someone is to manipulate or use them

explanation.surface: Soldiers out on morning manoeuvres keep themselves entertained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On manoeuvres' looks like army exercises; 'on' places the morning above the verb in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse someone is to entertain them, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Expert history teacher?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person highly skilled in something
second, playful meaning: one who teaches the past

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading, where history is the past and a teacher is a master.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a skilled adept, and literally suggests a schoolmaster of bygone times.

clue.text: Type of club responsible for great merriment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a choir singing part-songs

explanation.walkthrough: A glee is an unaccompanied part-song, and clubs formed to sing them are glee clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a kind of singing society and a noun for exuberant happiness.

clue.text: Stumped by peculiar name of part of flower

indicators.note: peculiar means odd or strange, so the word that follows is put in an odd order

parts.note: st. is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener baffled by the odd name of a bit of a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batter is stumped when the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket while they are out of their ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The stamen is the pollen-producing male organ of a flower.

clue.text: Sporting winter coats on lake

indicators.note: sporting can mean playful or frolicking, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: all thirteen letters of these words, used as fodder

explanation.surface: People wearing warm coats beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporting' looks like wearing; it is the anagram signal. Coniston Water is a lake in England's Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: This Cumbrian body of water, scene of Donald Campbell's speed records, is one of England's largest lakes.

clue.text: Non-starters for boy engaged in climbing

indicators.note: in a down answer climbing means reading upwards, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: a son is a boy
on means engaged or in use, as a phone line

explanation.surface: Nobody fancies a boy tied up in mountaineering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaged' looks like betrothed; here it means busy, as a telephone line is.
explanation.definitionFit: No-nos are things not to be done, so they are non-starters: ideas with no chance of going ahead.

clue.text: Book turns

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ... of the Apostles, a book of the New Testament
second meaning: performances in a variety show

explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb meaning reserve, and 'turns' like a verb; both are nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical book is titled this way, and stage turns are short performances or routines.

clue.text: Blessing boy is acceptable

parts.note: Ben is a boy's name
taken as written
on means acceptable, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: Giving one's approval to a son is a blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: Benison is an archaic or literary noun for a benediction or blessing.

clue.text: Small number very angry at one about vagrant

parts.note: no. is the short form of number
mad means furious
I is the Roman numeral one
c. (circa) means about, used with dates

explanation.surface: A few people are furious with someone over a tramp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small number' means an abbreviated number, not a few.
explanation.definitionFit: Vagrant as an adjective means wandering without a settled home, the same as nomadic.

clue.text: Direction of the asteroid

indicators.note: of here means made up of part of, so look within the following words

parts.note: letters running across the two words, thE ASTeroid

explanation.surface: An astronomer asks which way the asteroid is heading.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the four cardinal compass points, where the sun rises.

clue.text: Linkmen in crowd about to go in

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the crowd goes around the next idea

parts.note: a press is a dense crowd or throng
to enter is to go in

explanation.surface: TV hosts in a throng about to walk on set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to go in' reads as one phrase meaning ready to enter; 'about' is actually the wrapping signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A linkman is a broadcaster who introduces items and ties a programme together, as a presenter does.
